prize_parts.citation: For the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson, through the conception, construction and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider

statement.case_for: The discovery should come first, and the Higgs boson is the cleanest case on this list: the 2013 prize honoured the mechanism, and the particle itself, found independently by two detectors in 2012, has never been recognised. It is a decisive clue from nature rather than an elegant argument, and more than a decade of coupling and spin-parity measurements by both experiments has left the interpretation stable. Nothing else on the shortlist combines this level of fundamental importance with this level of confirmation. The attribution problem is real, but it comes from the size of the achievement and not from doubt about the discovery, and the three-person limit has forced hard choices before. A balanced trio from the two experiments (two ATLAS, one CMS, anchored in the founding leadership and the 2012 spokesperson role) is defensible.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the strongest reservation. Thousands of people made this discovery, any three names will be contested, and the committee may be reluctant to single out individuals in large collaborations. A three-person selection could look arbitrary, since it must choose between founders, 2012 spokespeople and ATLAS and CMS balance. The case for B031 is also cleaner: optical lattice clocks have a compact, uncontested credit line, so a committee that put attribution first would reasonably prefer Katori and Ye. The opening ballots show that my own first place has support from only two members, and I should not treat that as scientific merit.

responses.point: Pearce also ranks the Higgs experiment first and credits the founders Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee, with Gianotti as the 2012 ATLAS spokesperson a strong claim to be left for discussion.
responses.response: I agree that the founders should anchor the credit, and Jenni and Della Negra are in both of our trios. Where I differ is on Virdee versus Gianotti. Three of the other Higgs ballots, including yours, take two CMS founders and one ATLAS founder, which tilts the prize toward CMS. I prefer one name per experiment plus the founder Jenni, who has the longest continuous claim on ATLAS. I would still support the Pearce trio if the discussion settles on founders alone, since I regard the discovery as more important than the choice among the leaders. I do not think the 2012 spokesperson role should outweigh the years of detector building, but it is a real argument and I have not verified the precise dates of each role.

responses.point: Johansson ranks optical lattice clocks first as an original and lastingly important precision-measurement advance with a clean Katori and Ye attribution, and ranks the Higgs fourth because collaboration credit is arbitrary under the three-person rule.
responses.response: The clock is a strong candidate, and I agree its credit line is the cleanest on the list. But I am not persuaded that clean attribution outweighs fundamental importance. The clock refines how well we measure; the Higgs establishes the origin of mass for the gauge bosons and completes the Standard Model. Your own point about the 2005 comb and the 2012 ion-clock prizes shows a lineage that a lattice-clock award would extend rather than open. I would accept B031 as my fallback, and I take seriously that the redefinition of the second may strengthen its timing, but I would not put it above the Higgs.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks twisted bilayer graphene first as a simple mechanism predicted analytically and then confirmed, and prefers a two-laureate pair, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, while questioning whether Bistritzer should share the theory credit.
responses.response: I put B024 sixth and still think it is premature. The prediction is elegant and the experiment striking, but the origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, and I would like a clearer physical picture before a prize. On attribution I agree with you that Bistritzer and MacDonald published the continuum model together, so removing Bistritzer needs a strong argument. I find the two-name version harder to defend than three if the prize goes ahead. Cao, the first experimental author, is missing from the credited names under either option, which weakens the experimental credit.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks twisted bilayer graphene first as a prediction from continuum band theory meeting a striking experiment, and values the theory-experiment link most.
responses.response: I share your appreciation for a prediction followed by observation, and it is a more satisfying story than most. My reservation is the same as the one you list yourself: the pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample variation leave the central physics unsettled. Compare the Higgs, where the observation tested a precise prediction at the stated quantitative level. I would keep B024 among my alternatives and would re-rank it upward if the discussion produced evidence that the superconducting state is better understood.

uncertainties: Which three Higgs names best represent ATLAS and CMS, and whether founder roles or 2012 spokesperson roles should decide credit; I have not independently verified who held which role when.
Whether a large-collaboration discovery can be honoured with three individuals without it being read as arbitrary, which could push the committee toward B031.

Whether the committee will give the clock prize extra weight because six of eight members ranked it, and whether the prior comb and ion-clock prizes make lattice clocks an extension rather than a new discovery.
Whether the unsettled superconducting mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene is a decisive maturity barrier.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My supervisor David Gross and my co-author Thomas Van Riet have no connection to any shortlisted candidate that I am aware of, and my own research on string theory, dark energy and dark bubble cosmology does not overlap with the shortlisted work. My interest in black-hole alternatives is relevant only to B038, which I do not propose.
